text:
elaine: Quick ask — we need two distinct benchmark narratives for launch: a bite-sized social post (for fast conversion) and a webinar deep-dive (for platform/infra buyers). Core theme: translate latency differences into dollars and developer impact. Need recommended chart types, 2 headline options each, and routing/CTA guidance. Target: devs + platform leads. Due EOD Friday

mike: ok — propose 3 chart combos to pick from:
 - Scatter: latency (ms) vs cost-per-1k-tokens with iso-efficiency lines (shows tradeoffs)
 - Heatmap: throughput (tokens/sec) by model variant + quantization (easy visual for ops)
 - CDF (tail latency): % requests below X ms, emphasizes SLAs
For social use the scatter + short stat. For webinar open with heatmap then dive into waterfall cost breakdown.

sana: +1. Add a small routing diagram (fastpath/cheappath) for the landing page — shows automatic fallback to cheaper model when latency budget allows. For webinar demo: run a live 100-concurrent request test and show cost delta in real-time.

jordan: Recommend also a waterfall/stacked bar for unit-cost decomposition: infra, KV cache savings, batching, model flops. That helps explain where savings come from (not a magic number). One-liner headline ideas: "Same prompt, measurable savings" or "Latency you expect, cost you pay (but cheaper)"

ben: For inbound routing: create two CTAs on the landing page — "Try hosted benchmark" (self-serve) and "Talk to sales (Dedicated)" with an easy toggle for predicted TCO. Add UTM params for each segment. Also propose a lightweight qualifying form: company size + primary objective (latency vs cost) so SDRs can route.

marco: I mocked up 3 frames in Figma (link: figma.com/redwood/batch-demo — placeholder). Visual guidance: prefer high-contrast scatter + callouts on key clusters, and a simplified heatmap for social carousel. For colors, use teal for latency, amber for cost overlay.

elaine: Good — can someone draft the actual copy for the social post and webinar landing? Mike: social. Sana: landing + CTA copy. Also include alt copy for A/B headlines.

mike: Social draft (short):
"Benchmark: same prompt, 3x lower cost, 20% lower median latency. See how our routing + caching cuts token bills without sacrificing speed. Watch our live webinar for the deep-dive. ➜ link"
Variation (edgier):
"Faster responses. Smaller bills. Benchmark results in 90s. Join the webinar ➜ link"

sana: Landing headline (long form):
"Cut inference costs without trading latency — a playbook for engineers and infra teams."
Subhead: "Live benchmarks: scatter of latency vs cost, throughput heatmap, and unit-cost waterfall. Pick the model-routes that match your SLOs."
CTAs:
 - Primary: "Run a quick benchmark (hosted)"
 - Secondary: "Discuss Dedicated capacity"
Form fields: company size, use case, desired latency budget (ms).
A/B headline options: "Latency-first economics" vs "Cost-aware speed"

jordan: Landing copy tweak: call out sample numbers: "For a 1k-token chat prompt: typical infra cost $X vs optimized $Y (approx 40% savings)." Keep numbers conservative and link to appendix.

ben: Add auto-routing rules in the landing form: if company size > 1000 OR latency budget < 50ms then route to sales; else try hosted. Tag leads with "benchmark-interested".

marco: Visual notes for charts (to hand to design/data viz):
 - Scatter: x=median latency (ms), y=cost/1k tokens, point size=request throughput, color=model family. Add iso-lines labeled % cost reduction.
 - Heatmap: rows=model variants, cols=batch size/quant setting, cells=tokens/sec. Annotate common production configs.
 - Waterfall: stacked bars for cost-per-1k showing infra, batching benefit, KV cache, and model compute.
Keep all charts exportable as PNG/SVG for social and slide decks.

deploy-bot: FYI — scheduled webinar slot reserved: 2026-05-14 10:00 PT (ticket: #WB-234).

elaine: Nice. Next steps: mike + sana to deliver final copy + one-pager chart spec by Thu EOD; marco to hand off Figma frames; ben to draft inbound routing rules in a doc. I'll consolidate and send to design Friday morning. Thanks! :thumbsup:
